questions.question: Seven friends M, N, O, P, Q, R and S, each has scored different marks in the first semester examination. Only two people scored more than Q. P scored more than Q but less than O. M scored more than R but less than S. Only 3 students scored more than S. N scored the least among all. The scores of how many students are between the scores of P and R?
questions.solution:
*__**Seven friends:**__* M, N, O, P, Q, R and S.

1) Only two people scored more than Q.

**_ > _ > Q > _ > _ > _ > _**

2) P scored more than Q but less than O.

**O > P > Q**

3) M scored more than R but less than S.

**S > M > R**

4) Only 3 students scored more than S.

**_ > _ > _ > S > _ > _ > _**

5) N scored the least among all. 

**_ > _ > _ > _ > _ > _ > N**

Combining all the statements:

O > P > Q > S > M > R > N

Three students are between the scores of P and R.

Hence, the correct answer is **"3".**

questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All birds are cows.

Some cows are dogs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some dogs are birds.

II. Some cows are birds.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Statements:

All birds are cows.

Some cows are dogs.

The Venn diagram as per the given statements:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca18dec2cc6dda12d624e4b3dba78d051cc433b7cc4caa337c872ef321f9cbf2.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some dogs are birds. → **Not follow** (There is no direct relation between dogs and birds so it can be possible but not definitely true)

II. Some cows are birds. → **Follow** (Because all birds are cows, so some cows are birds is definitely true)

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusion II follows".**

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term.

26 : 375 :: 41 : 600 :: 53 : ?
questions.solution:
__LOGIC__: (First Number - 1) × 15 = Second Number

In 26 : 375 →

(26 - 1) × 15 = 25 × 15 = 375

And;

In 41 : 600 →

(41 - 1) × 15 = 40 × 15 = 600

Similarly;

In 53 : ? →

(53 - 1) × 15 = 52 × 15 = **780**

Hence, the correct answer is "780".

questions.question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

**Statements:**

No pumpkin is a guava.

No guava is a pea.

Some peas are potatoes.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some pumpkins are potatoes.

(II) Some peas are pumpkins.

(III) Some pumpkins are not potatoes.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows

questions.solution:
Statements:

No pumpkin is a guava.

No guava is a pea.

Some peas are potatoes.

The Venn diagram as per the given statements:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16b2d6ba95282a7ac14c099f86bf89b8b0227158d76cd8eeacda3009aa965c19.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some pumpkins are potatoes. → **Not follow** (There is no direct relation between pumpkins and potatoes so it can be possible but not definitely true)

(II) Some peas are pumpkins. → **Not follow** (Because no pumpkin is a guava and no guava is a pea so some peas are pumpkins is definitely false)

(III) Some pumpkins are not potatoes. → **Not follow** (There is no direct relation between pumpkins and potatoes so it can be possible but not definitely true)

Thus, the correct answer is "**None of the conclusions follows**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**"**Some**" and "**Some not**" are not the complementary pair hence, it is not a case of **Either-or**

Conditions of Either-or case:

 

1. The elements should be the same in both statements.

 

2. Both conclusions should be false individually.

 

3. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

 

The two complementary pairs are:

1) All + Some not; 

2) No + Some
